criteria.description: Every factual claim traces to code or a cited doc section; numbers (counts, timings, caps) match the code as of the stated alignment date.
criteria.name: accurate claims

criteria.description: Every major part of the system appears — layers, run lifecycle, traps, worker pool, scheduling, state on disk, portability, honest limits — and each section covers its topic, not just its heading.
criteria.name: complete coverage

criteria.description: At least one concrete worked example shows the real shape — code a reader can copy and run, with the rules that make it work stated beside it.
criteria.name: worked example

criteria.description: The page states what is not built and where the design stops, in the same voice as the rest — no section reads as if the system had no limits.
criteria.name: limits stated

criteria.description: Known gaps are named explicitly, with what is unknown and what would settle it — a gap the page hides is a gap the reader inherits.
criteria.name: known gaps

criteria.description: Every diagram is labeled, captioned, and explained in the surrounding text — a reader who cannot see the diagram still gets the point from the caption.
criteria.name: diagram clarity

criteria.description: The page can be navigated by section — sticky navigation, anchors, and headings that say what each section answers.
criteria.name: sections navigable

criteria.description: The page states who it is for and what background it assumes, so a reader can tell in the first screen whether it is written for them.
criteria.name: audience stated

criteria.description: Prerequisites are stated — what the reader is assumed to know before starting, and where to go if they do not know it.
criteria.name: prerequisites stated
